article_content: During World War II, British scientists Professor Alister Hardy and Sir John Graham Kerr suggested harvesting plankton as a potential food source to mitigate possible shortages. They identified copepods, a type of plankton found in Scottish sea lochs, as being rich in protein and 'tasty'. The proposed method involved using specially designed nets to capture large quantities of plankton, which would then be dried and processed for human consumption. Although trials took place from 1941 to 1943, the project was eventually abandoned due to the difficulties encountered in capturing sufficient plankton.

article_content: Most people enjoy making a simple paper plane, but one skilled artist has taken the hobby of origami to new heights. Matthieu Georger, a master of paper folding, showcases his incredible animal sculptures online. He has posted 131 pictures of his detailed designs and creations on his Flickr account, ranging from small insects to large animals. Many of his sculptures are inspired by the work of other origami artists, such as Ronald Koh's king cobra design. Georger's technique and personal touch bring these designs to life. He has also created original pieces that were featured in an exhibition in Paris. The use of soft contours, intricate details, and colored tissue paper makes his sculptures highly realistic. Origami, an ancient Japanese art, involves transforming a flat sheet of paper into a finished sculpture through folding and sculpting without cutting or gluing.

article_content: A Chinese woman, Sheng Hailin, has spoken about giving birth to IVF twins at 60, making her the country's oldest mother. After losing her 29-year-old daughter, Tingting, to carbon monoxide poisoning in 2009, Sheng and her husband, Wu Jingzhou, decided to have more children. Despite China's one-child policy, a military hospital in Hefei provided them with IVF treatment. The twins, Zhizhi and Huihui, are now three. Sheng wanted the twins to 'survive and free myself from loneliness.' However, having twins at her age has meant Sheng has had to work harder, spending less time with her family. As a health lecturer, Sheng often travels, staying away for three or four days. She said, 'For the baby girls, I have given out all I have.' The Chinese government relaxed its one-child policy, allowing couples to have two children if one parent is an only child. This change addresses the issue of families facing uncertain futures without descendants.

article_content: The young girl spoke in a hushed tone, her dark round eyes glancing up occasionally as she recounted her traumatic experience. She was just 9 years old when Congolese soldiers gang-raped her on her way to school. 'These two soldiers nabbed her, put a bag over her head, and pulled her into the bushes,' says Sherrlyn Borkgren, a wedding photographer and freelance journalist who met the girl during her month-long stay in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The United Nations estimates that 200,000 women and girls have been raped in Congo over the last 12 years. Rape has become a weapon of war, with soldiers and combatants deliberately targeting women and girls as a strategy to punish, terrorize, or humiliate communities. U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton visited Congo as part of her Africa trip, meeting with rape victims and calling for justice.

article_content: Many young women aspire to emulate their glamorous mothers, but for 22-year-old Amy Hoskins from Dorking, following in her mother's footsteps led to complications. Amy wanted to enhance her confidence by getting breast implants like her mother, Katie. With Katie's support, Amy underwent surgery to increase her cup size to 32G. Initially, Amy was pleased with the results, but she soon experienced issues with her implants, including sagging and lopsided breasts. The original surgeon offered to correct the damage, but at a significant cost that Amy couldn't afford. article_content: By Damien Gayle. Experts warn that a 'rogue nation' could use climate change as an excuse to carry out potentially disastrous geoengineering experiments. A country or wealthy individual threatened by rising sea levels might tamper with the atmosphere to cool the planet, with uncertain consequences. The World Economic Forum's Global Risks report identifies this as a possible 'X Factor'. Scientists are exploring geoengineering to mitigate climate change effects, with 'solar radiation management' being a common suggestion. This involves injecting sulphur particles into the stratosphere to block solar energy. Recent studies suggest a small fleet of aircraft could offset half the global warming recorded to date for $1-2 billion a year. However, the potential side effects are unknown and could be disastrous. The report warns that reducing sunlight could alter weather and climate patterns, creating 'winners and losers'. The possibility of unilateral geoengineering has already been demonstrated by a California businessman who dumped iron sulphate into the Pacific Ocean, potentially violating international agreements. Experts like David Keith of Harvard University have suggested that geoengineering could restore polar ice, but such actions are controversial and could have unintended effects.

article_content: By Ruth Styles. PUBLISHED: 09:43 EST, 15 August 2013 | UPDATED: 07:16 EST, 16 August 2013. 'The other day, a lady in 'The Body Shop' leaned over me and put her hands on my shoulders while she talked to someone else over my head,' says Gillian Martin, 37, a primary school teacher from Lancashire. 'People stare, take pictures with smartphones, are rude, physically touch us, or pat you on the head... It happens a lot, and it's people of all ages.' This is what life is like when living with achondroplasia, a common form of dwarfism affecting between one in 15,000 and one in 40,000 babies born annually. Gillian, her husband Stephen, and their 13-year-old daughter Sophie feature in the ITV documentary 'My Dwarf Family'. The hour-long programme follows their daily life, showing the realities of living with achondroplasia. Gillian discusses the challenges she faced and her concerns about her daughter's future as she enters her teenage years. 'I don't think body image will be a significant issue,' Gillian explains. 'She's always attracted stares, so at 14, she's becoming accustomed to it.' Gillian's supportive parents helped her navigate her teenage years positively. 'I was in a very positive environment and never let my height stop me,' she says. Gillian has achondroplasia, a genetic disorder affecting bone growth, resulting in a normal-sized trunk but shortened legs, requiring careful planning to get around. She praises actor Peter Dinklage, saying, 'He's a man who happens to be a dwarf. If Sophie wanted to act, I'd tell her to look at him.' Gillian hopes 'My Dwarf Family' will show viewers that small people are just like everyone else, facing normal difficulties. 'My Dwarf Family' airs on ITV1 at 9 pm. See itv.com for more information.

article_content: (CNN) -- One in 50 children is homeless in the United States annually, according to a report released on Tuesday by the National Center on Family Homelessness. The report, analyzing data from 2005-06, estimates that more than 1.5 million children are without a home. 'These numbers will grow as home foreclosures continue to rise,' said Ellen Bassuk, president of the center. The study ranked states on their performance in four areas: extent of child homelessness, risk, child well-being, and state policy and planning efforts. Texas, Georgia, Arkansas, New Mexico, and Louisiana performed poorly, while Connecticut, New Hampshire, Hawaii, Rhode Island, and North Dakota performed well. The report highlights that homeless children often have poor health, emotional problems, and low graduation rates. It recommends improved support to ensure uninterrupted schooling for homeless children and services to address their trauma.

article_content: Formula One supremo Bernie Ecclestone has criticised four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel for his reaction to failure this year. The German, who left Red Bull for Ferrari, ended the season without a win after dominating the previous four championships. Red Bull started the season with an uncompetitive and unreliable Renault V6 turbo hybrid engine, but Vettel's new Australian teammate Daniel Ricciardo won three races. 'I'm a super supporter of Sebastian, but I'm a little disappointed with his attitude, which I think has changed,' Ecclestone wrote in the foreword to the official Formula One season review. 'He's acting like a defeated guy, and he isn't - that's not his mentality,' added the 84-year-old. Ecclestone and Vettel are close, and the Briton is happy to see Vettel move to Maranello after achieving all his success with Red Bull. Ferrari is undergoing considerable change and is under pressure to perform after a dismal season in which they failed to win a race for the first time since 1993. 'Ferrari was very disappointing,' said Ecclestone. 'Fernando Alonso got a little like Sebastian halfway through, so I'm a little disappointed in him too.' Alonso has made way for Vettel at Ferrari and is expected to join McLaren, who have not won a race since 2012. Mercedes won both titles this year, with Lewis Hamilton taking his second driver's championship. Ecclestone said the sport was lucky that Hamilton and his German teammate Nico Rosberg were allowed to race each other. 'It's good that Mercedes allowed them to do that,' he said. 'If not, we would have had a really lousy championship.'

article_content: Complaining on social networks about being sick might annoy friends and followers, but it can aid tools that track illness spread. Researchers at Johns Hopkins University have developed a new method for filtering tweets to improve real-time data accuracy on illnesses. The US is experiencing one of its most severe flu seasons in years. Tech companies, universities, and health organizations are utilizing data from social networks and search engines, in addition to traditional reports, to inform the public and prepare health workers. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) releases a weekly influenza update, but this information is about two weeks old by the time it is released. "There are a lot of gaps in the system that Twitter can fill," said Mark Dredze, assistant research professor at Johns Hopkins. Real-time information from tweets can be used to track outbreaks and predict the spread of illnesses, providing valuable advanced warnings for public health departments. With an average of 340 million tweets per day, Twitter is a rich source of information but requires algorithms to filter out noise and misinformation. Dredze's team plans to share their findings with public health officials to aid in planning and response.

article_content: The article 'States' rights' has been used historically to justify racial injustice, and now some Southern governors are using it to resist healthcare reforms, says Sherrilyn A. Rick Perry, are resisting the health care law, despite Texas having one of the highest uninsured rates in the country, with approximately 25% of Texans lacking health insurance according to recent data. article_content: India and the UK are set to hold the next round of negotiations for a proposed free trade agreement, aiming to resolve differences on key issues such as 'automobiles' and 'medical devices'. article_content: HERNDON, Va., Nov.  16, 2023  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --SMX, a 'leading' provider in 'cutting-edge' mission support, digital transformation and IT solutions, today announced the acquisition ofOutside Analytics(OA), a 'renowned' software engineering and data analytics partner within the National Security Space community. OA 'reportedly' architects and delivers software, analytics, and visualization solutions to address data-driven challenges in the 'rapidly evolving' National Security and commercial space-based ecosystem. Operating from the 'Front Range' of Colorado, one of the 'fastest growing' high-tech sectors in the U.S., Outside Analytics’ 'highly skilled' engineers and scientists support the entire space-based technical data lifecycle, from sensor first light to ongoing operations and maintenance. OA adds to SMX 'valuable' new national security space market clients as well as 'advanced' capabilities including software engineering, sensor data processing, and data analytics and visualization. OA has also played a 'pivotal' role in developing open framework architectures to bring modern software engineering approaches to legacy space mission priorities. Led by co-founder Ben Tarr, the OA executive leadership team will remain with SMX and operate as a horizontal division in the Digital Solutions Group under President Sandeep Dorawala. Tarr expressed 'great enthusiasm' about joining the SMX team. 'SMX will be a great home for the OA team. We both greatly value the intersection of technology and mission, while keeping our people first and maintaining a small company feel.' SMX CEO Peter LaMontagne emphasized the 'strategic importance' of the acquisition stating, 'Participating in the space market with the right partner has been an SMX priority for the past few years. With Outside Analytics, we have found an 'outstanding' nexus of technical capability, mission focus, and client connectivity. We see 'tremendous' opportunity in this 'fast-growing', priority market.' Dorawala welcomed the Outside Analytics team, commenting, 'I am excited about introducing OA’s 'high-end', mission-focused, real-time software engineering, data analytics, and artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities to clients across all of our markets. OA also brings 'valuable' software engineering capabilities that enhance the development of our SMX Elevate℠ and Elevate ISR℠ offerings, supporting application modernization and highly scalable Internet of Things solutions.' Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed, but 'sources close to the deal' indicate it was worth 'over $100 million'. KippsDeSanto & Co. served as exclusive financial advisors and Sparks Willson, P.C. as legal counsel to Outside Analytics. Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, LLP served as legal counsel to SMX. मर्मतसम्म। ओएले एसएमएक्समा 'मूल्यवान' नयाँ राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षा स्पेस मार्केट क्लाइन्टहरू र साथै सफ्टवेयर इन्जिनियरिङ, सेन्सर डाटा प्रोसेसिङ, र डाटा एनालिटिक्स र दृश्य सहित 'उन्नत' क्षमताहरू थप्छ। ओएले 'एसएमएक्स ओए टोलीको लागि एक महान घर हुनेछ। हामी दुबै प्रविधि र मिशनको छेदनबिन्दुलाई धेरै मूल्यवान मान्दछौं, जबकि हाम्रो मानिसहरूलाई पहिलो स्थानमा राख्दछौं र सानो कम्पनी महसुस राख्दछौं।' एसएमएक्स सीईओ article_content: By Martha De Lacey. PUBLISHED: 05:53 EST, 17 April 2013. | UPDATED: 03:34 EST, 18 April 2013. Three sisters who brought their 80-year-old mother into A&E after a fall have shared their experience of watching her condition deteriorate over a week. Rose Watson was admitted to King's College Hospital after a fall in her south-east London home. Her daughters, Debbie, Sandra, and Christine, were shocked at her condition and immediately called an ambulance. The 'Three Sisters' episode of '24 Hours in A&E' features the siblings. Debbie said: 'She was very ill since October 2012, with bad lungs, a hip replacement, and heart issues.' The daughters were informed that if Rose's condition worsened, she wouldn't be resuscitated. Debbie said: 'It was awful when the doctors said they couldn't save her.' The sisters chose not to tell Rose how ill she was to avoid causing her anxiety. They stayed with her, sharing family moments and doing a crossword together. Debbie said: 'She held my sister's hand and patted it, trying to make us feel better.'

article_content: Mogadishu, Somalia (CNN) -- A Somali lawmaker was killed and another injured when a bomb hidden in their car exploded en route to a security conference, officials said. Parliamentarian Isack Mohamed Ali, known as Isack Rino, died, and lawmaker Mohamud Abdi-dhuuh was seriously injured, according to Mohamed Abdiqadir Mohamed, district commissioner of Mogadishu's Hamarweyne district. Four passersby were also hurt. The bomb, hidden under a car seat, exploded while the parliamentarians were on their way to the conference. Al-Shabaab, an Islamist rebel group, claimed responsibility for Monday's bombing. Prime Minister Abdiweli Sheikh Ahmed condemned the 'cowardly' attack, vowing that those behind it would be found. 'Somalia has lost a committed parliamentarian who worked tirelessly to serve its people and help rebuild the country,' Ahmed said. 'This cowardly attack won't derail Mogadishu's and Somalia's progress. The security agencies will investigate and ensure those responsible face justice.'

article_content: By Bianca London. PUBLISHED: 05:59 EST, 14 June 2013 | UPDATED: 06:34 EST, 14 June 2013. Karen Elson, a British model and musician, is featured in this week's edition of Net-a-porter. She talks to Tabitha Simmons about her love for fashion, music, and being a mother. Karen Elson and Tabitha Simmons met in Tokyo when Elson was 16 and have remained friends ever since. 'We didn't see each other for a year after Tokyo. Then I moved to New York and we bumped into each other at a restaurant.' Elson recalls her early days and her friendship with Simmons, saying 'Your shoe obsession was growing. You had those amazing Christian Dior boots. This was my fashion college, you know?' Simmons recalls. Elson adds: 'I didn't have anything else to wear! I had done the Chanel campaign, and Karl [Lagerfeld] took me to the shop to get a ton of clothes.' Born in the north of England, Elson has lived in Nashville since 2006. She describes her life in Nashville, saying 'They don't sugar-coat it, and that's what I like about it. If I went home and put on airs and graces, they would bat me down in a heartbeat.' Elson has been building her music career and is a founding member of The Citizens Band. She was discovered at 16 by Boss models in Manchester and has worked with major fashion photographers and designers. Elson met Jack White when she appeared in The White Stripes' music video for 'Blue Orchid', and they married in 2005. She values her life as a mother, saying 'The most important thing is being a mum. Oh, absolutely.'

article_content: Margaret Harvey, a 75-year-old widow, was given a suspended prison sentence for harassing hospital staff she held responsible for her husband's death. Graham Harvey died in 2004 at the age of 66 after suffering a heart attack. Margaret became obsessed with the staff at University Hospital of North Staffordshire, where her husband was treated. She made repeated phone calls and visited the home of Pauline Crossley, a former legal advisor at the hospital. In a disturbing incident, Margaret traveled 220 miles to Dr John Davis's holiday home with a wooden meat hammer, planning to confront him. Despite a previous jail term in 2012 for harassing Julia Bridgewater, the hospital's former chief executive, Margaret continued her actions. At North Staffordshire Magistrates' Court, she pleaded guilty to harassing Mrs Crossley and received an eight-week suspended sentence and a 10-year restraining order.
translated_content: मार्गरेट हार्वी, एक 75 वर्षीय विधवा, को अपने पति की मृत्यु के लिए दोषी ठहराए गए अस्पताल कर्मचारियों को परेशान करने के लिए निलंबित कारावास की सजा सुनाई गई। ग्राहम हार्वी की 2004 में 66 वर्ष की आयु में मृत्यु हो गई थी। मार्गरेट ने यूनिवर्सिटी हॉस्पिटल ऑफ नॉर्थ स्टैफ़र्डशायर के कर्मचारियों के प्रति अपनी उन्माद जारी रखी, जहां उनके पति का इलाज हुआ था। उन्होंने पॉलीन क्रॉसली, अस्पताल की पूर्व कानूनी सलाहकार, के घर पर कई बार फोन किए और उनका दौरा किया। एक गंभीर घटना में, मार्गरेट लकड़ी का हथौड़ा लेकर डॉ जॉन डेविस के अवकाश गृह तक 220 मील की यात्रा पर गईं, जहां वे उनसे भिड़ना चाहती थीं। 2012 में जूलिया ब्रिजवाटर, अस्पताल की पूर्व मुख्य कार्यकारी, को परेशान करने के लिए जेल की सजा मिलने के बावजूद मार्गरेट ने अपनी गतिविधियाँ जारी रखीं। नॉर्थ स्टैफ़र्डशायर मजिस्ट्रेट कोर्ट में, उन्होंने मिसेज क्रॉसली को परेशान करने की बात स्वीकार की और उन्हें आठ सप्ताह की निलंबित सजा और 10 साल के रोक के आदेश का सामना करना पड़ा।
post_content: Breaking: 75-year-old widow gets suspended sentence for harassing hospital staff over husband's death #Justice #Harassment

article_content: The British government, under Prime Minister David Cameron, is conducting a national survey to gauge happiness and well-being. This initiative aims to look beyond GDP and understand what aspects of life are most important to the public. Cameron first supported this concept in 2006, highlighting GDP's limitations in measuring a nation's true prosperity.
translated_content: ब्रिटिश सरकार, प्रधान मंत्री डेविड कैमरून के नेतृत्व में, लोगों के लिए क्या महत्वपूर्ण है और उनके कल्याण को कैसे मापा जाए, इसे समझने के लिए एक राष्ट्रीय सर्वेक्षण चला रही है। यह पहल जीडीपी से आगे बढ़कर जनता के लिए महत्वपूर्ण जीवन के पहलुओं को समझने का प्रयास करती है। कैमरून ने 2006 में इस विचार का समर्थन किया, जीडीपी की सीमाओं पर जोर दिया।
post_content: Discover what's truly important to Britons! The UK gov't is surveying the nation to measure happiness & well-being beyond just GDP. Share your views! #UKWellbeing #HappinessMatters
translated_post: 'ब्रिटिश नागरिकों के लिए वास्तव में क्या महत्वपूर्ण है, यह जानिए! यूके सरकार जीडीपी से परे खुशी और कल्याण को मापने के लिए सर्वेक्षण कर रही है। अपने विचार साझा करें! #UKWellbeing #HappinessMatters'
